piezas.titular: Three passes. Nobody asked to see them.

clips.escena: Macro shot of a welder running a root pass in an open steel butt joint, welding helmet down, face not visible, leather gloves. The arc travels slowly left to right as a small white point of light, molten pool following. Camera static.
Same steel joint, fill pass over the root, welding helmet down, leather gloves, slightly wider framing, gentle weave motion of the electrode. Camera drifts in very slowly.
Same steel joint, cap pass, welding helmet down, leather gloves, the finished stack of weld beads visible below the torch. Slow push in.

Gloved hands resting beside a finished three-pass weld on a steel plate, cooling, no arc, no spark, no glow anywhere. One thumb runs along the bead. Camera slowly tilts up from the weld. No face in frame.
clips.sub:
Three passes.
Nobody asked to see them.

piezas.copy:
Root. Fill. Cap.

Then someone reads one page of paper and decides whether you can weld.

On Bears LinkUp the profile leads with what you run and where you run it — process, position, finished work. The people hiring read that before they call.

piezas.titular: 6G no es un título. Es una posición.

clips.escena: Tight shot on a fixed steel pipe joint at 45 degrees, welder mid-bead, welding helmet down, face not visible, leather gloves, long sleeves. The arc is a small white point of light. Camera holds still.
Wider shot revealing the 45-degree angle of the fixed pipe and the welder's body twisted to reach it, welding helmet down, leather gloves, long sleeves. Slow orbit to the right.
Low angle under the fixed pipe, the welder reaching around the bottom of the joint, welding helmet down, leather gloves. Small white arc light, heat shimmer. Camera static.
A completed weld around a steel pipe circumference, cooling on a stand in a shop, no arc, no spark, no glow, no people in frame. Camera slowly orbits the pipe.
clips.sub:
No es un título.
Es una posición.

piezas.copy:
Tubo fijo a 45 grados. El que la ha corrido sabe por qué duele.

Y en un resumé se escribe igual que cualquier otra línea.

En Bears LinkUp la posición va en su propio espacio del perfil, donde la ve quien busca exactamente eso.

piezas.titular: They call for the price. Not the work.
piezas.foto: A finished steel handrail and stair stringer, freshly fabricated, standing on the clean concrete floor of a small metal shop. Grinder marks and mill scale visible, no paint yet. No people in frame. Soft daylight from a side door. The metal is the whole subject.
piezas.copy:
"What's the cheapest you can do it for?"

When that's the first question on every call, you're being shopped on price, not hired on work.

On Bears LinkUp the customer sees your finished jobs — gates, railings, stairs, structure — before they ask for the estimate.

clips.escena: Three welded steel test coupons lying side by side on a steel workbench, each with a different weld bead. No arc, no spark, no glow, no people. Camera slides slowly right across all three.
A printed resume on a clipboard on a steel workbench, a hand holding a pen taps once on a line. Hands only, no face, unreadable blurred text. Soft side light. Camera static.
A hand drawing a pen line through names on a printed list on a desk, unreadable blurred text, hands only. Camera slowly pushes in on the crossed-out lines.
Slow pull back from a steel workbench revealing welded test coupons and a clipboard together, the shop falling into darkness behind. No people.
